disk_gb.description: Requested instance filesystem size in GB. Omit for the platform default (100 GB), which never narrows placement. Setting it is a hard requirement: placement narrows to capacity that can honor it (see `disk_configurable` on GET /v1/pricing), and a request no offering of the gpu_type can honor returns 422 `disk_unavailable` rather than launching with a different size. Disk beyond the included allowance (100 GB) is billed at the offering's `disk_price_per_gb_hour` (GET /v1/pricing), folded into the instance's single hourly rate. Bounds: at least 10, at most the platform ceiling (currently 1000) — outside them returns 422 `validation_failed`.

env.description: Per-deploy env overrides; only keys the template marks user_overridable are accepted (others 422). Secret values are redacted from operation metadata.

environment.description: Launch environment. Omit for the provider default (the GPU.ai Certified Image where supported). Accepted values: `certified` (the GPU.ai Certified base image), `certified:<framework>` (a framework layer — see GET /v1/environments for the roster, e.g. `certified:pytorch`), `certified:<framework>@<version>` (a specific framework version, e.g. `certified:pytorch@2.13`), `raw_vm` (root VM, provider default OS), `raw_vm:<os>` (root VM with a chosen OS, e.g. `raw_vm:ubuntu-24.04`), or `provider_template` (the provider's own image). A well-formed value the placed machine can't serve returns 422 `environment_unavailable`.

max_price_per_hour.description: maximum acceptable whole-instance hourly price (catalog price)

offering_id.description: Pin the launch to one exact offering (from GET /v1/pricing) so the engine never substitutes a pricier one. If that offering is gone, the launch fails explicitly rather than silently placing elsewhere.

template_id.description: Deploy a curated application template (e.g. comfyui, vllm). When set, gpu_type may be omitted — the cheapest eligible GPU is auto-selected.

OpenAIForbidden.description: API key lacks the required scope (OpenAI error envelope).

OpenAIGone.description: The requested artifact has expired and is no longer available (OpenAI error envelope).

OpenAINotFound.description: Model or resource not found (OpenAI error envelope).

OpenAIRateLimited.description: Rate limit exceeded (OpenAI error envelope). Retry-After header indicates seconds to wait.

Retry-After.description: Seconds the client should wait before retrying.

OpenAIUnauthorized.description: Missing or invalid API key (OpenAI error envelope).

OpenAIUpstreamTimeout.description:
Upstream provider exceeded the synchronous per-attempt deadline (OpenAI
error envelope). 504 semantic — distinct from 503 OpenAIUpstreamUnavailable
which signals a connection or routing failure rather than a timeout.

OpenAIUpstreamUnavailable.description: Upstream provider unavailable (OpenAI error envelope). Retry-After header may indicate seconds to wait.

Retry-After.description: Seconds the client should wait before retrying.

OpenAIVideoList.description: A page of video generation jobs.

RateLimited.description: Rate limit exceeded (RFC 7807). Retry-After header indicates seconds to wait.

Retry-After.description: Seconds the client should wait before retrying.

model.description: Canonical (gpuai/...) model id, NEVER the upstream HF path.

CommunityMachine.description: A self-declared Community Cloud machine. Spec fields are optional and unverified until Phase 57. The enrollment token hash is never serialized.

tier.description: Supplier-chosen rental model. on_demand = guaranteed whole-node capacity; spot = cheaper interruptible capacity. Defaults to on_demand. Becomes the catalog offering's tier.

CommunityMachineDelistResult.description: The terminal status a machine reached after a delist. `draining` means it was occupied and the existing rental keeps running (never killed); `delisted` means it was idle and left supply immediately.

enrollment_token.description: One-time enrollment token — shown exactly once, store securely.

CommunitySupplier.description: One organization's Community Cloud supplier profile (ONBD-01).

CreateFineTuningJobRequest.description: Request body for POST /fine_tuning/jobs. The `method` object carries the Axolotl LoRA/QLoRA hyperparameters; `gpuai` is a native extension for the optional budget cap and GPU preference. The backing training environment (image, GPU provider) is an internal orchestration detail and is intentionally absent from this schema (privacy-by-omission, D6).

model.description: An operator-curated tunable base model id.

training_file.description: The id of a previously uploaded file (purpose=fine-tune).

CryptoDeposit.description: A stablecoin deposit. Mirrors the Go DTO field for field. Like that struct, this schema deliberately has NO payment-processor property — the processor is an implementation detail and is structurally absent from the customer contract, not merely filtered out.

amount_usd_cents.description: The amount requested, in USD cents. Never the settled or credited value.

credited_cents.description: USD cents actually credited to the balance. Absent until credited.

expires_at.description: RFC3339 UTC. After this, send nothing to pay_address.

pay_address.description: The address to send funds to. Unique to this deposit.

pay_amount.description: The exact token amount to send, as a decimal string (never a number — the value must not round-trip through a float).

status.description: Lifecycle state: created, detected, confirming, settled, screening, held_screening, credited, credited_underpaid, credited_overpaid, expired, expired_received, failed, failed_screening.

frameworks.description: Certified framework ids whose images are fully published — the `certified:<framework>` options.

includes.description: "What's included" software lists: framework id (roster ids plus "base") → CUDA variant ("cuda128"/"cuda124") → components.

versions.description: The version picker roster: framework id → selectable versions (the `certified:<framework>@<version>` grammar). A framework absent here has one build per CUDA variant. `variant` is the CUDA variant a version targets — only offerings whose GPU maps to it can run it.

vm_images.description: The raw-VM OS catalog (the `raw_vm:<os>` grammar), keyed by os id.

FileObject.description: An uploaded file object. The storage location is an internal detail and is intentionally absent from this schema (privacy-by-omission, D6).

FineTuningJob.description: The fine-tuning job object. `status` is the COLLAPSED public enum (the rich internal states are hidden). `result_files` are freshly-presigned, short-lived download URLs regenerated per read. No backing-provider identity is present (D6).

fine_tuned_model.description: Null in this release (catalog auto-serve is a later phase).

finished_at.description: Unix timestamp (seconds) at terminal state; null until terminal.

default.description: Preselected in the picker (at most one per framework).

cpu_cores.description: Representative host vCPU count for this GPU model. Unlike vram_gb (invariant per model) this varies per offering, so it is the first-sighting/typical value; GET /v1/pricing carries the exact per-offering spec. 0 marks a spec the upstream did not report.

disk_configurable.description: true when at least one offering of this model accepts a custom disk_gb at launch (an OR across offerings — requesting disk_gb narrows placement to the capable capacity).

instance_disk_gb.description: Representative instance filesystem size (GB) a launch of this model receives — the platform default where the upstream honors a configured size, otherwise the machine's reported disk; varies per offering — see cpu_cores. 0 marks an unreported disk (unknown, not zero). GET /v1/pricing carries the exact per-offering value.

ram_gb.description: Representative host RAM (GB) for this GPU model; varies per offering — see cpu_cores. 0 marks an unreported spec.

storage_gb.description: Representative host storage (GB) for this GPU model; varies per offering — see cpu_cores. 0 marks an unreported spec.

model.description: Customer-facing image model id (e.g. gpuai/flux.1-schnell) or alias.

n.description: Number of images to generate. Defaults to 1.

prompt.description: Text description of the image(s) to generate.

response_format.description: Only b64_json is supported. A value of "url" is rejected with invalid_request_error until S3-backed URL delivery lands.

created.description: Unix timestamp (seconds) when the response was created.

image_count.description: Number of images generated (the billable unit).

version.description: Resolved build version; absent for unpinned components (e.g. git).

app_url.description: HTTPS URL of the deployed application (template instances only), e.g. https://gpu-abcd1234.apps.gpu.ai.

disk_gb.description: Instance filesystem size in GB that the platform configured for this launch. Present only where the placed capacity honors a configured disk size; absent means the machine's disk is provider-determined (its own flavor volume).

price_per_hour.description: hourly rate for the whole instance — covers all gpu_count GPUs

status.description: Customer-facing lifecycle status. "allocating" = the GPU is still being acquired from the provider (slow-boot capacity such as baremetal can take ~15 min); "starting" = the node exists and is booting; "running" = ready to use.

parameters.description: Typed parameter descriptors for media (image/video) models — name, type, enum/bounds/default. Playgrounds render input forms from these.

default.description: Default value for the field (any JSON scalar).

per_image_microcents.description: Exact per-image rate in micro-cents (1e-6 cent). Prefer this for image models — per_image_cents rounds sub-cent prices to 0.

per_mpxl_microcents.description: Price per output megapixel in micro-cents (1e-6 cent) for image models metered per megapixel. Mutually exclusive with the per-image fields.

per_video_microcents.description: Representative per-clip price in micro-cents (1e-6 cent) for video models — a "from" price taken from the provider's published example rate.

per_video_second_microcents.description: Exact per-second-of-output-video rate in micro-cents (1e-6 cent). Prefer this for video models.

type.description: OpenAI error class (e.g. invalid_request_error, authentication_error, billing_error).

result.description: Terminal-success payload. For template deploys this carries the one-time app credential — returned by GET /operations/{id} exactly once; never on GET /instances/{id}.

available.description: count of available units, summed across merged identical offers

capacity_class.description: per-offering capacity classification — "secure" for datacenter-operated hardware, "community" for supplier/peer-hosted hardware with a softer SLA. The string twin of `community`, classified per offering rather than per upstream. May transiently be empty for cache entries written before the field existed.

community.description: true when this offering is community-supplied capacity

cpu_cores.description: host vCPU count for this offering, tied to the shown (cheapest) price. 0 marks an unreported spec.

disk_configurable.description: true when a launch of this offering may choose its own disk size via the create request's disk_gb. A distinguishing field in the offer merge — configurable and fixed-disk capacity for the same SKU stay separate rows.

disk_price_per_gb_hour.description: Retail price of one GB of instance disk beyond instance_disk_gb, per hour, for launches of this offering. A launch requesting disk_gb above instance_disk_gb is billed approximately price_per_hour + (disk_gb − instance_disk_gb) × disk_price_per_gb_hour (the exact billed rate folds disk into one cent-rounded hourly price). 0 when the offering is not disk-configurable, or when disk above the included allowance is currently free.

gpu_count.description: number of GPUs in the listed configuration

instance_disk_gb.description: Instance filesystem size (GB) a launch of THIS offering receives — the platform default where the upstream honors a configured size, otherwise the machine's own reported disk; tied to the shown (cheapest) price like cpu_cores. 0 marks an unreported disk (unknown, not zero).

instant_boot.description: true when instances of this offering are typically reachable within about a minute of launch; false for capacity with longer provisioning times (~3-5 minutes)

price_per_hour.description: hourly price for the whole listed configuration — covers all gpu_count GPUs

ram_gb.description: host RAM (GB) for this offering, tied to the shown price. 0 marks an unreported spec.

storage_gb.description: host storage (GB) for this offering, tied to the shown price. 0 marks an unreported spec.

RegisterCommunityMachineRequest.description: All fields optional; an empty body registers a zero-spec placeholder in pending_verification.

tier.description: Supplier-chosen rental model. Optional; omitted resolves to on_demand. spot lists the machine as cheaper interruptible capacity.

include_usage.description: When true, the final stream chunk carries usage totals (CHAT-03).

Template.description: A deployable application template. The container image (registry path) and start command are internal orchestration details and are intentionally absent from this schema (TMPL-13 defense-by-omission).

kind.description: Deployable kind. "service" is a long-running app exposed at connection.app_url. "finetuning" is a run-to-completion job (no app_url) and is currently advertised only as a coming-soon catalog entry — not yet deployable.

driver_preinstalled.description: true when the image ships the NVIDIA driver + CUDA baked in.

model.description: Customer-facing video model id (e.g. gpuai/wan-2.2-t2v) or alias.

prompt.description: Text description of the video to generate.

seconds.description: Output video duration in seconds (the billable unit).

completed_at.description: Unix timestamp (seconds) when the job completed.

cost_cents.description: Final billed cost in cents; present once the job completes (failed/cancelled jobs are never billed).

created_at.description: Unix timestamp (seconds) when the job was created.

error.description: Canonical failure code when status is failed.

expires_at.description: Unix timestamp (seconds) when the artifact expires (24h after completion).

secret.description: Returned ONLY at creation; subsequent reads omit.

info.description:
Programmatic API for GPU.ai. Authenticate with API keys minted from
the dashboard. See https://gpu.ai/docs for details.
info.title: GPU.ai Public Developer API

get.description: Returns the organization's stablecoin deposits, newest first, capped at 50. Requires the `billing:read` scope. The organization is taken from the authenticated API key, never from a parameter. Returns 404 when stablecoin deposits are not enabled for this deployment.

post.description: Creates a deposit intent and returns the payment address and the exact token amount to send. Requires the `billing:write` scope; any member of the organization may add funds. Send the exact `pay_amount` of `asset` on `chain` and no other network — funds sent on a different network are not detected automatically. Returns 404 when stablecoin deposits are not enabled for this deployment.

amount_cents.description: Amount to deposit in USD cents. Must be at least the configured minimum (500 = $5.00 by default).

400.description: `validation-error` — `amount_cents` is below the configured minimum. `unsupported-chain-asset` — the chain/asset pair is not available. `invalid-request` — malformed JSON body.

403.description: `org-frozen` — the organization cannot add funds; contact support.

503.description: `payment-source-unavailable` — deposits are temporarily unavailable; retry shortly.

get.description: Returns a single deposit belonging to the caller's organization. Requires the `billing:read` scope. A deposit belonging to another organization returns the same `404 deposit-not-found` as one that does not exist — deliberately, so this endpoint cannot be used to test whether a deposit id is real. Also 404 when stablecoin deposits are not enabled for this deployment.

404.description: `deposit-not-found` — no such deposit, or it belongs to another organization. `not-found` — the feature is not enabled.

get.description: Returns the organization's monthly spending limit and opt-in daily spend cap, with the current month and day spend. Requires the `billing:read` scope. Returns 404 when no limit is configured.

put.description: Sets the monthly spending limit and optionally sets or clears the opt-in daily spend cap. Requires the `billing:write` scope AND org-admin privileges (a non-admin member gets 403). `daily_limit_dollars` uses pointer semantics: omit to leave the cap unchanged, 0 to clear it, a positive value to set it.

auto_terminate_hours.description: Hours after the limit is reached before auto-terminate; null = never.

daily_limit_dollars.description: Opt-in daily cap in USD. Omit = unchanged, 0 = clear, > 0 = set.

schema.description: Server-Sent Events stream of ChatCompletionChunk objects, terminated by `data: [DONE]`.

200.description:
Successful response. application/json for non-streaming requests;
text/event-stream for streaming requests (stream=true).

post.description: Registers a self-declared machine under the caller's community supplier and mints a one-time enrollment token. All spec fields are optional — an empty body registers a placeholder in `pending_verification`. The `enrollment_token` is shown exactly once and never returned again. Requires the `community` scope (or `full_access`).

201.description: The registered machine plus its one-time enrollment token.

403.description: The community supplier role is suspended.

409.description: The community supplier role has not been enabled yet.

post.description: Removes a machine the caller's org owns from supply (ONBD-04). Drain-not-kill: an occupied machine becomes `draining` (its customer rental keeps running until it ends naturally) and an idle machine becomes `delisted`. The endpoint never force-terminates a running rental. A missing or cross-org machine returns 404 with an indistinguishable body so existence never leaks across orgs. Requires the `community` scope (or `full_access`).

200.description: The terminal status the machine reached.

403.description: The community supplier role is suspended.

404.description: The machine does not exist or is not owned by the caller's org.

409.description: The community supplier role has not been enabled yet.

post.description: Idempotently enables the Community Cloud supplier role for the organization the API key belongs to. A repeat call is a no-op that returns the same supplier record (200, not 201). Requires the `community` scope (or `full_access`).

200.description: The community supplier record (created or already-existing).

post.summary: Enable the Community Cloud supplier role

get.description: Returns the community supplier record for the organization the API key belongs to, or 404 `not-a-supplier` when the role has not been enabled. Requires the `community` scope (read).

404.description: The organization has not enabled the community supplier role.

get.summary: Get the caller's Community Cloud supplier

get.description: The server-controlled launch environment catalog — the certified framework roster, the selectable version(s) per framework (the version picker), the "What's included" software lists, and the raw-VM OS catalog. These are exactly the values accepted by the `environment` field of POST /v1/instances.

200.description: A page of fine-tuning job events.

get.summary: List available GPU types (no auth required)

post.description: Synchronous text-to-image generation. Returns base64-encoded images only (`response_format` is restricted to `b64_json`); a value of `url` is rejected with `invalid_request_error` until S3-backed URL delivery lands. Pass an `Idempotency-Key` header to make a retried request replay the original response without a second charge.

get.description: Lists the organization's instances. By default terminated instances are excluded; pass status=terminated for the history or status=all for everything.

parameters.description: Filter by customer-facing status (default = all non-terminated)
parameters.name: status

post.summary: Create an instance (async — returns 202 + Operation-Id header)

delete.description: Members can terminate only instances they created; organization admins can terminate any instance in the organization.

403.description: Forbidden — members can only terminate instances they created

patch.summary: Update an instance (rename only in v1)

get.description: Lists every distinct offer (gpu_type, gpu_count, region, tier, price, boot class). Customer-identical offers are merged with availability summed. Offers with zero availability are omitted unless include_unavailable=true.

parameters.description: Exact-match filter on canonical region code
parameters.name: region

parameters.description: Include offers whose current availability is zero
parameters.name: include_unavailable

get.summary: List pricing per GPU type + region (no auth required)

get.description: Returns the SSH keys owned by the user the API key was minted by. Org-wide key visibility is an admin capability in the dashboard.

delete.summary: Delete an SSH key (idempotent — 404 on already-gone per D-07)

post.description: Submit an asynchronous text-to-video generation job. Returns a job object with status `queued`; poll GET /videos/{id} until `completed`, then stream the result from GET /videos/{id}/content. Pass an `Idempotency-Key` header to make a retried request replay the original response without a second charge.

get.description: Streams the generated MP4 for a completed job. Returns 410 Gone once the artifact has expired (24h retention).
